audit.why: FAVOURED 4/10 fits 51.6% over 1372 games and a dash-reset melee against an immobile caster with no dash in kit. Full-layer sides and content win[] already agree on all seven rows (Irelia), and packet.levelChart matches both, so no chart edit was needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike named an ability that does not exist: 'Devastating Visions', 'Baleful Gaze', 'Fated Fates/Fatal Reckoning', 'Severalty'. packet.defects already recorded that the matchup never names a real Hwei ability.
audit.why: The real names are Signature of the Visionary (P), Subject: Disaster (Q, 10/9/8/7/6s -> Devastating Fire, Severing Bolt, Molten Fissure), Subject: Serenity (W, 18s), Subject: Torment (E, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s -> Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss, Crushing Maw) and Spiraling Despair (R, 120/100/80s at 1300 range).
audit.corrected: Every fabricated name replaced with the real one, with the palette cooldowns attached.

audit.whatIsWrong: The placeholder 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' stood in for the ability name in nine fields, and the passive's actual mechanic was never stated. whys[2] also called Irelia's W a shield.
audit.why: Signature of the Visionary primes on the first damaging spell and completes on the SECOND, then detonates — so the counterplay is never eating two casts, which nothing on the page said. All of Hwei's crowd control genuinely does live on Subject: Torment, so its 12s downtime is the whole green light. Irelia's Defiant Dance is physical damage reduction, not a shield, and does close to nothing against Hwei.
audit.corrected: Subject: Torment named throughout, the two-spell signature rule stated, and the W corrected to physical-only mitigation.

audit.why: Subject: Torment 12s->10s, Subject: Disaster 10s->6s, Subject: Serenity 18s->16s, Spiraling Despair 120s.
audit.corrected: Written in with the move-on-Torment-downtime rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, and spikes[2] claimed a '70% to dead' burst with nothing behind the number.
audit.why: Lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED plus a magnitude with no source.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to their titles; the invented percentage removed.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are close because Hwei's poke range and Devastating Visions zone control let him chip you if you walk up carelessly, but his cast times are slow enough that you can walk-up-and-back to bait a spell before committing your Q. Play patient, farm with auto-attacks, and don't let him free-cast on your face.

Play patient, farm with autos, and never eat two spells — the second one is what completes his signature.

edits.before: From level 3 onward Irelia takes over completely — Bladesurge into Defiant Dance shreds through anything Hwei paints on the ground, and by 6 Vanguard's Edge lets you close the last gap and stun him even through a Baleful Gaze attempt. His kit rewards distance and punishes commitment, but Irelia's dash-reset kit removes distance as a variable, so every level from 3 to 6 you should be looking for all-in windows whenever he over-extends a combo.

notes: This matchup carried more fabricated ability names than any other in the slice: 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' (a template placeholder appearing in nine fields), plus 'Devastating Visions', 'Baleful Gaze', 'Fated Fates', 'Fatal Reckoning' and 'Severalty' — none of which exist. All replaced with Subject: Disaster / Subject: Serenity / Subject: Torment / Spiraling Despair / Signature of the Visionary and their sub-spells. Two lint-adjacent report entries still carry the old placeholder and were left under the two-report cap: report[3].t ('Great trade: Hwei wastes Subject: Fear (CC Paints)') and report[9].t ('Commit on Subject: Fear (CC Paints)'s cooldown'). Both need the same swap to Subject: Torment in a later pass — they are the last two places the placeholder survives.
